hint_records.scope_evidence: Handles both large-number conversion directions and derives the exponent from the actual decimal movement rather than a hardcoded count.
Handles both small-number conversion directions with the correct negative exponent magnitude and leading zeros.
Normalizes before comparing, then separates a notation task from an exponent-first magnitude comparison.
Multiplies coefficients, adds signed exponents and renormalizes while preserving value.
Divides coefficients, subtracts denominator exponent and compensates the exponent correctly for coefficient movement in either direction.
Branches between products and quotients and renormalizes coefficients both above and below the allowed interval.
Rewrites the smaller-exponent term at the larger exponent with a smaller coefficient, performs the requested signed operation and normalizes.

Aligns exponents before addition/subtraction and compensates the exponent in both directions. Earlier rung explicitly excludes coefficient ten. Final rung now explicitly states coefficient at least one and strictly less than ten, matching the canonical half-open interval.
Uses repeated multiplication and preserves only appropriate contextual units, avoiding a universal square-unit claim for pure numbers.
Finds and squares back the nonnegative candidate and distinguishes an area-to-length context from unitless evaluation.
Tests a principal root by ordinary multiplication, avoiding a requirement to use an unintroduced binomial expansion.
Evaluates principal roots before the actual arithmetic or contextual step, including subtraction and perimeter multiplication.
Takes principal numerator and positive denominator roots separately, simplifies the fraction and verifies by squaring.
Supports both multiplying known roots and solving for a missing positive product factor through division.

Uses the exact squared midpoint between consecutive candidate roots. This gives the genuine nearest-integer boundary and handles a stated tie rule; it avoids the unsafe general nearest-square-distance shortcut.
Requires nonnegative competitors before squaring and distinguishes ordered original expressions from selecting one extreme.
Recognizes a candidate from three equal factors and verifies by cubing rather than multiplying a displayed root by an unrelated number.
Uses the actual fourth/fifth index and distinguishes the nonnegative principal even root from a signed odd real root.
Requires complete square extraction, either largest square or repeated extraction to a squarefree remainder.

template_records.scope_evidence: Every displayed literal numerator is k² for k=1..12. The positive denominator 169=13² gives principal root k/13. Prime denominator 13 exceeds every numerator k, so each fraction is reduced; squaring returns exactly the original radicand.
